text:
Now stripping all four probes and the bisect config:

Fixed and deployed — tap away.

**Root cause:** every tap in the simulator was arriving with ⌘ and ⇧ reported as *held down* — a stuck hardware-keyboard modifier (your CleanShot screenshot chord is ⌘⇧-something, and the sim's keyboard passthrough latched it). Those taps silently fell into the desktop **multi-select** branch, which has no visual effect on mobile — hence "tap and nothing happens." It was never the keyboard plugin; the crash-reload I saw in the logs was a red herring.

**The fix:** on mobile, taps now always plain-select — modifier-click semantics (⌘ multi-select, ⇧ range-select) are desktop-only branches. So the app is immune to this even on real devices with hardware keyboards. Pressing ⌘ and ⇧ once inside the simulator window also unsticks the latched state, for what it's worth.

Also cleaned up: all four debug probes removed, the log/dev servers killed, and the keyboard-resize bisect reverted — so the keyboard accessory toolbar behaves as designed again (docks above the software keyboard; toggle it with ⌘K in the sim to see it).

Still buried — so in this WKWebView the visual viewport doesn't shrink either (the nav plugin's view hierarchy again). Stop inferring: the keyboard plugin **tells us the keyboard height directly** via its native events, regardless of what any viewport does. Wiring that as the primary signal, viewport as fallback:

Now the bar consumes the native signal first, viewport as fallback:

Deployed — try it now (tap into the entry text with the software keyboard on).

The fix this round: the bar mounts lazily on focus, but `keyboardWillShow` fires *while the component's chunk is still loading* — so its subscription always started too late and the offset stayed 0 (behind the keyboard). The keyboard listener now lives in the bridge, subscribed once at app startup, and maintains a `--kb-height` CSS variable on the page; the bar simply pins to `bottom: var(--kb-height)`. No component timing involved — the variable is already correct before the bar ever mounts. This signal also can't be defeated by the native-nav re-parenting, because UIKit keyboard notifications are app-global.

If it *still* doesn't appear, the next probe is one line (log the var's value), but I expect this one lands.

text:
That round is already deployed — the agent finished with the bundled build running on your simulator, so no rebuild needed from me.

The gist of what it found and fixed, because it's the systemic version of several bugs you'd hit: **every bottom sheet was being covered by the keyboard** whenever a page autofocused an input (Location, Tags, Manage trackers — your screenshot exactly), and the per-sheet `bottom` fix from earlier was being silently overwritten by vaul's inline styles at runtime. The durable fix is one global rule in `mobile.css`: every vaul drawer lifts by `--kb-height` (with `!important` to outrank vaul, animated, 0 at rest), plus a max-height clamp so lifted sheets can't push their header off-screen, and the trackers manager no longer summons the keyboard on entry. All verified with on-device screenshots at each step: Location, Tags, Manage trackers, and Add link all fully visible above the keys now.

Two housekeeping notes from its report worth knowing:
- It caught a real bug in the `mobile:ios:live` script — `CAP_SERVER_URL` only applies to `cap sync`, then `cap run` regenerates the config without it, silently breaking live reload. Left untouched as out of scope; cheap to fix whenever you want.
- Its testing accidentally stamped your "Friday, July 3" test entry with the simulator's GPS location; it reverted the file (a "New York City" entry may linger in location recents).

Everything remains green: typecheck, 0 lint errors, 78/78 tests, both builds, desktop untouched. And the offer stands — the whole mobile MVP is one big uncommitted tree; when a full pass on the sim feels right, I'll slice it into clean commits.

text:
All of that round is already deployed and simulator-verified by the agent — nothing for me to rebuild. The highlights worth knowing:

- **The true root cause of the sheet/keyboard fights** finally has a name: vaul's `repositionInputs` (on by default) reacts to the keyboard with math that assumes Safari's resizing viewport — in the Capacitor webview it computed garbage, collapsing the search sheet to a sliver and clobbering our `bottom` offsets. It's now disabled on mobile (the app owns keyboard handling via `--kb-height`), which hardens *every* sheet, and the shared height clamp now respects the native navbar too.
- **A pre-existing production crash was caught and fixed**: tapping the Date row crashed into the error boundary — `showPicker()` throws in WKWebView when called outside user activation. Every mobile date edit would have crashed in production; it's now guarded and the calendar still opens.
- **Date row** keeps its settings-row shape while editing (label left, compact date pill right), and **search** opens correctly: input pinned under the navbar, results scrolling, sheet docked above the keyboard.

The embedded desktop component (with its hover-only, touch-invisible controls) is gone, along with its `embedded` prop.
- **The Location page got the grouped-card treatment** — 48px "Use current location" accent row (pulsing while detecting), search + suggestions as one card with hairlines, danger "Remove location" row.
